faq_heading: Chilliwack Proper South: your questions answered

blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. This section was written from City of Chilliwack, Canadian Encyclopedia, Canadian Register and school district pages, and replaces text that was repeated on the other Chilliwack guides.
Where Chilliwack Proper South sits on the City's maps

Chilliwack Proper South is a real estate sub-area name, not a City neighbourhood. The City's Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island plan splits the area around downtown into four planning areas: Mountainview to the east, Riverside to the north, Townsend to the west, and Fairfield Island across the Hope Slough. None is labelled south. The Townsend description names Ashwell and Evans Road as the arterial to Highway 1, so a home near Evans Road will probably be read under that part of the plan. Confirm it by address.

The City's neighbourhood profile treats Chilliwack Proper, downtown included, as the core urban neighbourhood. It counts 31,410 residents in 2021, about 31 percent of Chilliwack, up 14 percent from 27,650 in 2011, with a median age of 40.8. It covers more ground than the MLS sub-area, so treat it as backdrop rather than a count for your street.
From Centreville to the city you see today

The Canadian Encyclopedia gives the name as Ts'elxwéyeqw, which Elder Albert Louie says in Halq'eméylem means going as far as you can go upriver by canoe on the Chilliwack River. The township of Chilliwhack was incorporated in 1873. The Centreville subdivision followed in 1881, and in 1908 Centreville became a city and took the name Chilliwack. The township and city reunited in 1980, and the district municipality became a city in 1999.

The former City Hall at 45820 Spadina Avenue is the easiest piece of that history to visit. Built in 1910 to 1912 in the Neoclassical Revival style, it became the Chilliwack Museum, which the Historical Society says opened there on March 21, 1987.

blocks.text: Mostly bungalows from the 1950s to the 1980s

Across the plan area the City says building began in the 1950s and ran through the 1980s, and that the housing is mainly single-storey detached bungalows. Roofs, wiring, plumbing and drainage of different ages can sit on one block, so ask about each.

blocks.text: What the plan allows, and what the flood rules limit

The plan sets three residential designations. Res-1 covers detached homes, duplexes, coach houses or garden suites and secondary suites. Res-2 adds narrow-lot houses, rowhouses and townhouses. Res-3 covers townhouses and low-rise apartments, including apartments of 51 m² or less near frequent transit. Height is capped at 10 m, or 17.5 m for apartments. The plan calls basement suites not appropriate because of floodplain restrictions and suggests a coach house or garden suite instead.

The City's 2019 suite guide says a secondary suite must be under 40 percent of the habitable floor area or 90 m², whichever is less. A suite, coach house or garden suite generally needs three parking spaces on the lot, two of them unenclosed, and coach houses need a Development Permit under Development Permit Area 10. A suite is legal only if the zone allows it and it was built under a permit. The guide is several years old, so ask the City whether anything has changed.

Under Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 4519, habitable floors in areas behind a standard dike must sit at the Flood Construction Level plus 0.6 m of freeboard. The City's residential guide says basements are not permitted in general floodplain areas, though a crawlspace up to 1.5 m deep is. The bylaw text names the Fraser, Chilliwack and Vedder floodplains and not Chilliwack Proper, so I could not confirm the status of any street here. Check the City's online mapping or call Development and Regulatory Services at 604-793-2905. Ask for the permit history of any finished lower level.
Townsend Park and everyday green space

Townsend Park is a 15-hectare park west of downtown. The City lists five multipurpose pitches (three lit), six lit softball diamonds, an all-weather turf field, a play area, change rooms and a concession. A perimeter trail of about 2.3 km is made up of a 1.3 km loop and a 1 km loop. The site plan references Wolfe Road and Ashwell Road, and field bookings go through the Operations Department at 604-793-2904. If you are looking at a house beside the fields, visit on a game day first to see the parking and noise for yourself.
Getting around by bus and by car

BC Transit's route 52 Evans runs between Cottonwood Mall and Downtown Chilliwack, with timing points at Evans Rd at Yale Rd and Hodgins Ave at Ashwell Rd. Weekday times run from 6:06 am to 11:35 pm, with 17 trips towards downtown. Route 57 Broadway links the same two ends via Young Rd at Olds Dr and Yale Rd at Menzies St, with 16 weekday trips. Check the timetable for the hours you need, and test any commute by car at your actual hours too.
Condo buildings in Chilliwack Proper South

Classification conflict flagged at the top. Feed-source conflict flagged. The live page's FAQ states its listings "update directly from the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board MLS® feed," while Chilliwack is a CADREB market per CADREB's own territory description — which feed actually supplies the page is UNVERIFIED. No SnapStats for Chilliwack.
The Vibe — 45555, 45559, 45561 and 45567 Yale Road

Strata plan BCS2854. A four-storey building offering 220 condos, quality built by Rempel Development Group in 2008, at Yale Road and Airport Road; the development includes all four addresses, with exercise studio, billiards room, library, business centre, meeting rooms and fireplace lounge, and secured underground parking in its directory record. Directory restrictions: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed. Individual listings differ slightly by phase address on year (2007–2009 across the four addresses) — the directory's 2008 date for the complex is followed here, with the per-address variation flagged. Current listings label the address Chilliwack Proper South and classify units Apartment/Condo, freehold strata in listing records.
The Elliot — 45562 Airport Road

Apartment/Condo building labelled Chilliwack Proper South in current listings, subdivision name The Elliot, frame-wood construction with fibre-cement, mixed and stone exterior in a current listing, underground parking, and a rooftop patio described in that listing. The developer-side marketing page records the project as Type Condo, Status Complete, Sold Out, at 45562 Airport Road, Chilliwack, by Redekop Faye. Year built — CONFLICT IN SOURCES: listings state 2020 in some and 2021 in others (2020–2021 UNCONFIRMED). Unit count: UNCONFIRMED — no source checked publishes one. A current listing records pets: Cats OK — a listing note for that unit, not the registered bylaw; other published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Elmwood Terrace — 8725 Elm Drive

Apartment/Condo building labelled Chilliwack Proper South in current listings, described in listings as "55+ ELMWOOD TERRACE, a spotless, quiet community" with gym/games room and social area among its amenities, exercise centre, recreation facilities and sauna/steam room in listing amenity fields, built 1986. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED. Published restrictions beyond the listings' 55+ description: UNCONFIRMED — confirm the registered age bylaw on the Form B.
Streets, schools and getting around Chilliwack Proper South

items.t: Chilliwack Proper South is the south half of "Chilliwack Proper," the board grouping for the city-proper (downtown-side) part of Chilliwack, as distinct from the Sardis / Vedder / Garrison side south of Highway 1. The page works to the corridors Yale Road, Nowell Street, Spadina Avenue, Chilliwack Central Road and Young Road north of Highway 1. No board-published boundary for "Chilliwack Proper South" exists: UNVERIFIED as an official boundary — treat the corridor list as the page's working scope. Nearby areas: Chilliwack Proper East and Chilliwack Proper West on the same city-proper side, Fairfield Island to the north, and Sardis / Vedder Crossing south of Highway 1.
Municipality: City of Chilliwack, BC. CADREB's own territory description covers a regional area from Yarrow to Lytton including Chilliwack.
Audit note: the October 21, 2026 thin-content audit records this page as "mostly duplicate of chilliwack-proper-east.html (60.1%)" — a rebuild consideration, not a market fact.

Where the condo stock concentrates: Yale Road and Airport Road at the west end, and Elm Drive. The seven feed cards read in full for the research were condo-led — five low-rise condo units on Yale Road, Airport Road and Elm Drive, alongside a detached rancher-style unit in a 55+ gated community at 8500 Young Road and a detached rancher on Nowell Street — a more attached-heavy mix than the page's detached-led description (detached homes on 6,000+ sq ft lots, ranchers, townhome complexes, low-rise apartment condos, infill lots) suggests. The lot-size figure is the page's description, not an official statistic: UNVERIFIED as a measured profile.

Schools: SD33 Chilliwack serves the area; the district directs families to enter a street address in its School Locator to find the catchment school. District structure: SD33 has nineteen elementary schools (K–5), four middle schools (Grades 6–8), two K-8 schools and five secondary schools (Grades 9–12). Address-level catchments: UNVERIFIED — no locator result was run for a Proper South address.

Transit as the live page names it: BC Transit Routes 51, 52, 57 and 58 along Yale Road and Young Road, with connection to Route 66 Fraser Valley Express at the Downtown Exchange. Route-level confirmation on a BC Transit page in the research pass: UNVERIFIED.

Amenities as the live page names them: the Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre, Chilliwack Cultural Centre, Prospera Centre arena, Exhibition Field and Central Community Park; Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Road, is the community hospital for the city, providing primary, core secondary and some specialty services. Facility addresses/details on a City page: UNVERIFIED in the research pass for the recreation list.

blocks.text: Good to know about Chilliwack Proper South

items.t: The feed is condo-led even though the copy is house-led. Of the seven cards read in full for the research, five were low-rise condo units — the attached product is what actually moves through this page, whatever the detached-first description implies.

The page cannot agree with itself about which board feeds it. Its FAQ credits the Fraser Valley board's MLS® feed; CADREB's own territory description makes Chilliwack a CADREB market. Board identity matters because it decides whose statistics (here: none published at sub-area level) a buyer can ask for.

The Vibe's four addresses do not share one build year in listings. Phase addresses show 2007–2009 across listings against the directory's single 2008 for the complex — warranty and depreciation timing for a specific unit follows its own phase, not the marketing year.

The Elliot's marketing survived its sell-out. The project page still reads "Sold Out / Complete" with no unit count published — a buyer looking for the building's size or original disclosure material will not find it there; the Form B and strata plan carry it.
The school name in the page copy is not the Ministry name.

Chilliwack's suite cap is a "lesser of" test, not a flat number. A secondary suite must be both under 90 m² AND under 40% of the building's habitable floor space, inside a building with only one principal dwelling — and the one-ADU-per-lot rule means a legal suite forecloses a coach house on the same lot.

The tax penalty calendar is Chilliwack's own. 5% after July 2, 2026 and a second 5% after August 4, 2026 — a different second-stage date than the rural regime's October 31 and a different structure than Mission's flat 10%.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Chilliwack Proper South

items.t: OCP — frame carried with its research caveat: the program's standing position is that Chilliwack's current plan is the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500. A parcel's designation is a per-parcel City check.
Zoning: Chilliwack Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000

SSMUH (Bylaw 5395, adopted Jun 18, 2024): the City's small-scale multi-unit housing amendment to Bylaw 5000 allows 3 to 4 dwelling units on parcels within the urban growth boundary zoned for single-detached and duplex housing. Added-unit permission is NOT permission to subdivide and does not create new lots.

Secondary suites and accessory units (Bylaw 5000): a secondary suite is an accessory dwelling unit of not more than 90 m² and less than 40% of the habitable floor space of the building — the lesser of 90 m² and 40% (s.2); only 1 ADU may be located on a lot, and the permitted types include secondary suite, coach house and garden suite (s.4.06(1)); garden suites cap at a maximum gross floor area of 100 m²; ADU parking is addressed in s.5.04. The City's Secondary Suites Policy permits rental of suites within any single detached dwelling regardless of zone; a suite must be built with a building permit, meet the BC Building and Fire Code and current flood protection requirements, and new suites are not permitted below the flood construction level under the Floodplain Regulation Bylaw.

Short-term rentals (Chilliwack): STR operations are regulated under Short-Term Rental Bylaw 2021, No. 5141, which repealed the former Bed and Breakfast Bylaw 2003, No. 2968 — confirm a property can be licensed under it before valuing any rental income from a lot purchase.

ALR block (provincial frame — no sub-area ALR parcel is documented in the research, stated so it is not misapplied): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tier — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by Oct 31 — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR, and no farm-class claim is asserted for this sub-area.

Chilliwack property taxes (2026): notices mailed at the end of May, due the first working day after July 1; a 5% penalty applies to taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026, and an additional 5% to taxes outstanding after August 4, 2026.

Foreclosure / court-sale note: Where a court sale is met, the settled process is the BC Supreme Court process (Rules 21-7/13-5, PD-66, Form 60), with Form B availability and the PTT/GST treatment of court sales UNCONFIRMED and kept distinct from the GI-003 frame above. (Standing program frame)

faq.q: Is Chilliwack Proper South an official City neighbourhood?
faq.a: No. It is an MLS sub-area name. The City's plan uses four planning areas, Mountainview, Riverside, Townsend and Fairfield Island, and none is called south. Ask which one a specific address falls in.

faq.q: Which plan area covers the Evans Road side?
faq.a: The Townsend description names Ashwell and Evans Road as the arterial to Highway 1. That is the closest official description, but the City publishes no south boundary, so confirm by address.

faq.q: How big are the lots, and can I add a coach house?
faq.a: The plan gives typical existing Townsend lots as 600 to 1,000 m². Coach houses and garden suites are allowed in zones such as R1-A, need a Development Permit, and generally need three on-site parking spaces. Zoning is set lot by lot, so check first.

faq.q: Can I have a basement suite here?
faq.a: The plan says basement suites are not appropriate because of floodplain restrictions, and the City's residential guide says basements are not permitted in general floodplain areas. Ask the City about the exact address and whether any existing suite has a permit.

A 15-hectare park with five multipurpose pitches, six lit softball diamonds, an all-weather turf field, a play area, washrooms and a 2.3 km perimeter trail. Bookings go through the Operations Department at 604-793-2904.

faq.q: Which bus routes serve the area?
faq.a: Routes 52 Evans and 57 Broadway both run between Cottonwood Mall and Downtown Chilliwack. Route 52 has timing points at Evans Rd at Yale Rd and Hodgins Ave at Ashwell Rd. Check BC Transit for current times.
A.D. Rundle Middle School, at 45660 Hocking Avenue, serves grades 6 to 8. School District 33 sets catchments by address, so confirm with the district before you rely on one.

faq.q: Is there local history I can visit?
faq.a: The Chilliwack Museum is in the former City Hall at 45820 Spadina Avenue. Jean McNaughton Park, at 45951 Victoria Avenue, marks the site of the first courthouse, built in 1894.

faq.q: Which schools are near Chilliwack Proper South?
faq.a: Evans Elementary (7600 Evans Rd) and Robertson Elementary (46106 Southlands Cres), Kindergarten to Grade 5; A.D. Rundle Middle School (45660 Hocking Ave) and Chilliwack Middle School (46354 Yale Rd), Grades 6 to 8; and Chilliwack Secondary (46363 Yale Rd) and Imagine High Integrated Arts/Technology (45669 Yale Rd), Grades 9 to 12 — names and addresses confirmed against the BC Ministry K-12 file; catchments are set by address, so check the exact address with the SD33 School Locator (~/workspace/area-research-2026-11/education/work/bc_k12_schools.csv, read 2026-11-01).

faq.q: What condo buildings are in Chilliwack Proper South?
faq.a: Three verified by name: The Vibe (45555–45567 Yale Road, 220 units, 2008), The Elliot (45562 Airport Road, completed condo project by Redekop Faye, year 2020–2021 UNCONFIRMED) and Elmwood Terrace (8725 Elm Drive, 55+ in listings, built 1986).

faq.q: Why are there no market numbers for this area?
faq.a: Chilliwack trades on CADREB, SnapStats does not cover the city, and CADREB publishes board-wide figures only — any Proper South statistic is UNVERIFIED here rather than borrowed from a neighbouring board. Price from the property's own CADREB comparables.

faq.q: Is The Elliot a new building I would pay GST on?
faq.a: No, on the sources checked: its marketing page records the project as Complete and Sold Out, so units trade as resales and GST does not apply to a resale — confirm the specific unit's status (developer assignment vs resale) before relying on that. Its build year is itself unsettled (2020 vs 2021 across listings).

faq.q: Can I rent out a Proper South condo long-term?
Can I buy in Elmwood Terrace if I am under 55?
faq.a: The building is presented as a 55+ community in its listings. A 55+ bylaw is the one age bylaw BC law still allows (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2), with exemptions for legacy residents, live-in caregivers and (since May 1, 2023) younger spouses/partners and defined children — whether you can occupy depends on the registered bylaw on the Form B.

faq.q: What about Hazelwood Grove on Young Road — is that a townhouse complex?
faq.a: Not settled. Listings for 8485 Young Road variously record Row / Townhouse, Strata, and a rancher-with-loft duplex form, and the 55-plus program holds its age position UNCONFIRMED.

faq.q: Cottage Grove charges strata fees but the homes are detached ranchers — what am I buying?
faq.a: A detached rancher in a gated strata community (listings record a monthly strata fee and "Senior Community: Yes"; the complex is verified 55+ in the 55-plus program). Detached form does not mean non-strata: confirm the strata form and the registered 55+ bylaw on the title and Form B.

faq.q: Why is The Vibe in the Proper South file when it is on Yale Road?
faq.a: Because Yale Road buildings follow the current MLS sub-area labels: current listings label The Vibe's addresses Chilliwack Proper South and Newmark / Mountain View Estates Chilliwack Proper East.
